parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing restriction is documented: no border gender-marker screening, facility exclusion, birth-sex custody, or criminalisation of gender expression. Anti-discrimination law (Law 13/2019) covers gender identity in public establishments, and the 2025 healthcare decree is resident-facing. Negatives are real but local: a 2023 transphobic column (removed with apology), a documented parental expulsion, microaggressions underreported from fear, enforcement of bias-crime law incomplete, and no hate-crime registration. The 2–3/month bias count has no denominator and no trans breakdown, so it is not usable as a rate. Visitor-specific questions (document checks, police stops, facilities) are undocumented, not cleared. Rated in the Reduced band, below the 0.75 anchors because enforcement is partial and the record is thin on visitor-facing practice.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border gender-marker screening, mismatch detention or document refusal is recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented as a specific protection. Home-passport use means resident gender-recognition law is not a visitor protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents are issued at home; the 2022 Family Law is resident-facing and does not govern entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No detention, custody placement or identity-based search of visitors is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No custody rules for trans detainees are in the dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any detention would fall under general procedure, which is not described; this gap is an open question, not a cleared risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access or bathroom restriction appears; Law 13/2019 covers public establishments.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented in part: Law 13/2019 prohibits discrimination in public establishments on gender identity grounds. Operation is only partly evidenced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational variation is documented; the national anti-discrimination statute is the operative layer.

care_services.exposure: Documented limits: 2025 decree gives HRT from 16 and surgery from 18; under-16s get consultation coverage only. Microaggressions reported but rarely escalated.
care_services.protection: Documented: Law 13/2019 covers health care; ministry consultation on protocols in 2023.
care_services.interaction: The age limits bind minors and residents. A visitor seeking ongoing care would be unlikely to access public coverage, and that gap is not documented as applying to visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: a transphobic newspaper opinion piece (2023) framing trans identity as mental illness, later removed with apology. No official threat-framing is recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documented: removal and public apology after advocacy complaint; equality ministry measures.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Public hostility appears in media but official institutions responded to it. Harassment is underreported, so the record may understate it.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: parental expulsion over sexual orientation (undated, unlocated). Adolescent gender-affirming care is age-restricted; under-16 coverage is consultation only.
minors_guardians.protection: Documented: Law 14/2019 requires respect for transgender children's gender identity. Operation for visiting minors is not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's exposure depends on guardian and school contact, not on border rules, which are undocumented. The parental-expulsion record is local-sphere.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific street violence against visitors is documented. The bias-incident count (2–3/month) covers all motives with no denominator, so it cannot be read as a trans rate. A 2000 murder of a gay man is dated and sexual-orientation based.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented: bias-motivated offences attract enhanced penalties. Enforcement is incomplete and gender identity is not explicitly in the enhancement.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police record bias incidents, but no registration or classification system exists, so prosecution of trans-motivated violence is not traceable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Documented gaps: no hate-crime classification system; workplace harassment protocols do not address gender diversity; complaints rarely reach authorities.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented: anti-discrimination law (2005, Law 13/2019); equality ministry activity; apology and removal in the media case.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists on paper and has worked in at least one public case. Its reach for visitors (complaints, reporting) is not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that border and entry rules show no documented trans-specific friction and remedies exist for detention. This dossier documents no detention or border-discretion record at all, so it is not clearly better. It sits similar, slightly lower because visitor-facing practice is undocumented.

Lower operative exposure. The 0.55-B case documents routine secondary screening and denial of entry, which this dossier does not record. This case has no documented traveller-facing restriction, so it sits clearly higher.

Lower. The 0.85-A case has explicit identity-inclusive services, prompt discipline and a civilian oversight body. This dossier has anti-discrimination law but incomplete enforcement, no hate-crime classification and gaps in harassment protocols, so it sits below.

parsed.synthesis: No traveller-facing restriction is documented: no border document-mismatch practice, no facility exclusion, no custody rule and no criminalisation of gender expression. Documented positives (Law 13/2019, removal of a transphobic column, equality measures) operate in the public-establishment and media spheres. Documented negatives are local (parental expulsion, microaggressions underreported, adolescent care limits, no bias-crime classification). The large open questions (border checks, police stops, visitor detention) are unanswered, not cleared, and are weighted lightly. Overall the record supports a Reduced Risk rating with the main uncertainty being undocumented visitor-facing practice.
